title: KV cache + attention kernel seqlen edgecase debug scratchpad
content:
Quick personal notes / breadcrumbs while poking at this seqlen edgecase that seems to flip kernel selection and evict KV cache unexpectedly. Goal: capture commands tried, raw snippets, and hypotheses so I don't forget between context switches.

Summary:
- Symptoms: At ~seq_len ~ 2048 boundary (and sometimes at 2049), some requests are falling back to the slower attention kernel and we see KV cache misses + degraded p99 latency. Behavior is intermittent and correlated with certain batch/stream combos.
- Repro window: started seeing reliably on 2026-02-10 after the quantized-kernel roll (PR 612). Might be related to kernel heuristics that switch execution path based on max_seq_len and kv cache state.

How I repro locally (notes for myself):
- Baseline harness: tools/bench/run_inference_test.sh --model redwood-alpha-3b --batch 4 --seq 2048 --stream true --use-kv-cache true
- When I toggle --seq 2048 -> 2049 I can sometimes trigger fallback. Run the harness 50x in a loop to capture flaky behavior.
- quick repro loop: for i in {1..50}; do tools/bench/run_inference_test.sh --model redwood-alpha-3b --batch 4 --seq $((2048 + (i % 2))) --stream true --use-kv-cache true 2>&1 | tee out.$i.log; done

Commands & interesting outputs:
- Kernel selection debug env var: RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNELS=1
- Example output when fallback happens (snip from out.17.log):
  [2026-02-14T09:12:03.184Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=attention_naive fallback_reason=kv_cache_inconsistent max_seq_len=2048 observed_prefix_len=2049
  [2026-02-14T09:12:03.186Z] kv_cache: miss at shard=1 key_id=0x7f3a.. status=partial_eviction
  [2026-02-14T09:12:03.190Z] latency: token_generate p50=12ms p95=110ms p99=320ms

- Compare with success run (out.18.log):
  [2026-02-14T09:12:03.400Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=attention_optimized reason=kv_cache_consistent max_seq_len=2048 observed_prefix_len=2048
  [2026-02-14T09:12:03.402Z] kv_cache: hit all_shards
  [2026-02-14T09:12:03.405Z] latency: token_generate p50=8ms p95=22ms p99=40ms

Hypotheses so far (ranked):
1) Kernel switching heuristic uses observed_prefix_len (actual tokens in KV) vs configured max_seq_len. Off-by-one when streaming + partial flush causes observed_prefix_len to be 1 greater than expected, triggering naive kernel. Could be race between stream flush and cache append.
2) KV cache eviction policy: when batch contains mixed seq lens (one request 2048, another 2049) a shard-level compaction runs and marks status=partial_eviction which kernel selector interprets as inconsistent and falls back.
3) Quantized kernel (PR 612) changed alignment assumptions (block size 16/32) and pushes effective max_seq_len boundary up/down for kernel optimized path - combined with rounding it flips selection at boundary.
4) A bug in prefix/KV bookkeeping when using continuous batching + streaming: the prefix length metric is updated after kernel selection in some code paths, so selection sees stale prefix length.

Quick traces I grabbed (TODO: upload raw perf traces to S3):
- s3://redwood-logs/eng-runtime/debug/kv-seqlen/out.17.log  (fallback run)
- s3://redwood-logs/eng-runtime/debug/kv-seqlen/out.18.log  (fast run)
- perf: s3://redwood-logs/eng-runtime/debug/kv-seqlen/perf-20260214-0912.tar.gz

Relevant code areas to inspect (notes to self):
- runtime/kernel_selector.cc: function choose_kernel_for_request() - logic around prefix_len vs max_seq_len.
- runtime/kv_cache/shard_manager.cc: mark_eviction() + status flags.
- runtime/exec/attention_kernels/* : attention_optimized vs attention_naive heuristics. Also check quantized-kernel changes in PR 612.
- serving/streaming/stream_writer.cc: flush boundaries and when we append to KV.

Experiments run (results):
1) Force kernel selection to optimized (env RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=attention_optimized) -> no fallbacks, latency good, but correctness? Confirmed outputs match baseline for 50/50 runs. Means optimized kernel works at least for these cases.
2) Force kernel selection to naive -> always slower but stable (expected).
3) Disable streaming (--stream false) -> no fallback events across 200 runs. Suggests streaming interaction.
4) Small batch size 1 -> no fallback. Batch mixing seems contributory.
5) Patch: in kernel_selector add a small tolerance (if observed_prefix_len == max_seq_len + 1) treat as equal -> reduces fallbacks in local runs but need to reason about correctness and not mask real overflow.

Raw error snippets and logs pasted here for quick search: (grep-friendly)
- "fallback_reason=kv_cache_inconsistent"
- "status=partial_eviction"
- "observed_prefix_len=2049 max_seq_len=2048"
- "chosen_kernel=attention_naive"

Immediate next steps (short):
- [ ] Add assert/checks around prefix_len update ordering: log stack at time of kernel selection to see if prefix was updated immediately before/after. (Liam said he can help with the stack capture).
- [ ] Re-run with deterministic scheduler (tools/bench/with_helgrind.sh?) to try to force the race.
- [ ] Add unit test that simulates streaming append + kernel selection path to reproduce observed_prefix_len==max_seq_len+1. Can mock KV shard manager to set partial_eviction status.
- [ ] Check PR 612 diff for any changes to sequence rounding / block alignment constants.
- [ ] If patch-tolerance (max_seq_len+1) is applied, run longer e2e tests and perf regression tests on CI to ensure we don't regress memory / correctness.

Longer-term notes / considerations:
- If kernel selection is too conservative on partial_eviction, we pay p99 penalties for rare mixed batches. Consider implementing cheaper fast-path to revalidate KV consistency per-request rather than per-batch. Example: quick bloom filter / per-key checksum check before full fallback.
- If quantization alignment is flipping selection around boundary, we should encode alignment constants into kernel selection comparators so decision is deterministic and documented.
- Add more observability: emit metric kernel_selector.reason with tags {model, batch_size, stream_on, observed_prefix_len, max_seq_len} to search for real incidence rates in prod.

Notes to self about human comms:
- Send a short note to #runtime-debugging-thread with 1-sentence summary + link to this doc + the two s3 logs. Ask if Distributed Kernel folks have seen similar.
- Ticket ENG-3472 exists; add my experiments and link perf tarball.

Misc scratch ideas (not validated):
- Try making observed_prefix_len computed from KV logical length rather than number of appended tokens to avoid transient off-by-one during streaming flush.
- Consider marking partial_eviction transient for X ms: if kernel_selector sees partial_eviction but also observed_prefix_len <= max_seq_len, allow optimized kernel with a conservative fallback-on-failure path that can re-run naive kernel if verification fails. Might be okay for lower latency SLOs but need to test correctness.

Final quick checklist before I step away:
- [x] capture logs (done)
- [x] push notes to this scratchpad (current)
- [ ] create a small unit test (blocking until I chat w/ Liam)
- [ ] propose metric additions (open PR to telemetry)

If I forget: primary hypothesis = streaming + batch mixing can create a tiny window where observed_prefix_len is computed as max_seq_len + 1 while kv cache still marked consistent -> triggers naive kernel. Fix likely in ordering/race window or add small tolerance.
